channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Nunes Marques articula consenso no julgamento da AtlasIntel
item.description: TSE President Justice Kássio Nunes Marques is seeking consensus to establish a rule banning the use of audio and video in electoral polls, following the AtlasIntel survey of May 19 that showed a drop in Flávio Bolsonaro’s popularity after exposing him in an audio with Daniel Vorcaro. Despite a request for vista by Justice Estela Aranha, Nunes Marques and Dias Toffoli argue the case should set a precedent on polling methodologies to avoid inducing voter responses. The goal is to send a message to pollsters, campaigns, and regional electoral courts about media influence on 'useful voting' perceptions, with expectations of a majority to approve the rule even without full unanimity.

item.title: Lula pressiona Márcio França em um xadrez que envolve palanques para a eleição
item.description: Lula is pressing Márcio França to abandon his Senate bid and become Fernando Haddad’s running mate in São Paulo to resolve a conflict over two Senate seats contested by Marina Silva and Simone Tebet. The maneuver is part of a broader negotiation involving PSB support for Lula’s allies in Minas Gerais and Pernambuco, and the PSB’s concession of its party label to host Tebet’s campaign after she left the MDB. França has previously yielded to Lula’s pressure, sacrificing candidacies for ministerial posts, but now faces a more intricate political chessgame spanning multiple states.

item.title: PT aciona STF e PF contra ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) filed representations with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) and the Federal Police (PF) requesting an investigation into the funding of 'Dark Horse', a biopic about former President Jair Bolsonaro. The PT alleges that some of the film's financing may have been illicitly sourced, potentially involving money laundering or illegal electoral contributions.

item.title: Lula promete zerar fila do INSS até setembro
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced that the new INSS president, Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, pledged to clear the backlog of benefit requests by September 2026, following a 15.4% drop from April to May, reducing pending claims from 2.6 million to 2.2 million. The decline began in March, one month before Gilberto Waller’s dismissal, and may be linked to INSS Normative Instruction PRES/INSS No. 203, which bars duplicate applications. Lula reaffirmed his 2022 campaign promise, stating that staffing or competency gaps must be addressed through hiring or replacements.

item.title: Lula confirma promessa de zerar fila de pedidos represados do INSS antes da eleição
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva confirmed that the government will clear the backlog of INSS benefit requests by September, ahead of the 2026 elections. The announcement was made during a ceremony at the Planalto Palace, emphasizing social security as a key electoral priority.

item.title: Presidente do INSS prometeu zerar fila até setembro, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reiterated, during a ceremony at the Palácio do Planalto, the promise to clear the INSS benefits waiting list by September, as assured by the institute’s new president, Ana Cristina Silveira. The backlog, which reached a record 3.1 million in February, has long been tied to a 2022 campaign pledge. Lula emphasized the April leadership change, replacing Gilberto Waller with career servant Ana Cristina, to expedite the resolution.

item.title: Sem acordo sobre urgência, Motta cede e define relator de projeto do governo sobre o fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Chamber President Hugo Motta appointed Leo Prates as rapporteur for the government's workweek reduction project after failing to remove constitutional urgency. The government retained urgency on its bill, while Motta pushed forward with the previously approved PEC to avoid legislative blockage before the July recess. The conflict highlights a power struggle between the Executive and Legislative branches, with the government linking its stance to rural debt renegotiation.

item.title: Ministros tentam reaproximar Lula de Alcolumbre após avanço de pauta-bomba no Senado
item.description: Ministers and political leaders are seeking to reconcile President Lula with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre following their rift after the Senate rejected Lula’s nominee, Jorge Messias, for the STF. Defense Minister José Múcio Monteiro, a mutual friend, is mediating the effort, though Lula has yet to schedule a meeting. The push comes amid heightened tension due to Senate approval of fiscally impactful measures, including debt renegotiation for large rural producers (minimum R$140 billion/year for a decade), wage increases for doctors and dentists, and special retirement for health agents.

item.title: Férias de julho: pesquisa aponta quais são os destinos mais desejados
item.description: Gramado (RS) leads Brazilian search trends for July 2026 vacations, with more than double the searches of the second-place destination, followed by Northeastern beach destinations occupying six of the top ten spots. Internationally, Bariloche tops searches, with Ushuaia and Santiago highlighting winter travel interest and Punta Cana and Cancún maintaining Caribbean appeal, while Buenos Aires reflects sustained interest in major cities.

item.title: Lula diz que INSS tem meta de zerar fila de espera para concessão de benefícios até setembro
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced that the INSS aims to eliminate the backlog of benefit applications by September 2024, fulfilling a 2022 campaign promise. New INSS president Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, appointed in April after Gilberto Waller’s dismissal, oversees a decline in pending requests from 3.1 million in February to 2.2 million currently, with average processing time dropping from 59 to 40 days. The target excludes documentation-related delays by beneficiaries, which account for over 20% of the backlog.

item.title: Motta diz que votará projeto da 6x1 na terça e nega acordo com governo
item.description: Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies, said he will vote on the government bill to end the 6×1 work scale on Tuesday (June 16), but denied having made an agreement with the government to do so. He stated he will "unblock the agenda one way or another" if the government does not withdraw the constitutional urgency that is blocking other bills. Motta appointed the same rapporteur as the PEC 6×1, Leo Prates, and said the bill to be voted is the same text as the already approved PEC.

item.title: Motta anuncia relator do Projeto de Lei que acaba com a escala 6X1
item.description: Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies Hugo Motta announced that federal deputy Leo Prates will be the rapporteur of the bill to end the 6X1 work scale, maintaining the same text as the PEC already approved by the Chamber in May. The move aims to unblock the legislative agenda to advance on issues such as the Legal Framework for AI and increasing MEI revenue, with the workweek reduced from 44 to 42 hours within 60 days and to 40 hours within 14 months after promulgation.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro protocola notícia-crime no STF contra Lula por ameaça e incitação ao crime
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) filed a criminal complaint at the STF against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), alleging threats and incitement to crime. The document requests the opening of an investigation into the president's statements.

item.title: ‘Alcolumbre age como dono da bola’, diz cientista político sobre pauta-bomba no Senado
item.description: Political scientist Elias Tavares says the Senate's approval of 'bomb' proposals is a major headache for President Lula's government, as it increases public spending and pleases the opposition, especially agribusiness interests. He criticizes Senate President Davi Alcolumbre for acting like a 'ball owner,' using contentious proposals to pressure the Executive and block other legislation, despite warnings from the Finance Ministry about fiscal responsibility.

item.title: PT lança jingle para a Copa com slogan "Lula joga pelo Brasil"
item.description: The PT launched a pre-campaign jingle for Lula's re-election, featuring the slogan 'Lula plays for Brazil', linking football to national identity and the 2026 World Cup context. The video highlights government programs such as CNH do Brasil, Desenrola Brasil, Gás do Povo, Agora Tem Especialistas, and the Pix, while also criticizing U.S. tariff threats to Brazil's digital payment system.

item.title: Zanatta vice de Flávio?
item.description: Federal Deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) is being mentioned as a potential running mate for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the 2026 presidential race. According to O Antagonista, Zanatta has made herself available, but has not yet received a formal invitation from Bolsonaro. Her name is part of internal PL discussions regarding the formation of the majoritarian ticket.

item.title: Lula lidera cenários de 1º e 2º turnos em PE, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll conducted June 9–10, 2026 in Pernambuco shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) would win the presidential election in the first round with 57% of votes, ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 22%. In a hypothetical runoff, Lula would secure 60% versus Bolsonaro’s 34%, with Bolsonaro also being the most rejected candidate (54%) and Lula at 32% rejection.

item.title: Lei reconhece ofício das quebradeiras de coco babaçu como manifestação cultural
item.description: Law 15.431, signed by President Lula, recognizes the work of babaçu coconut breakers in the states of Tocantins, Maranhão, Piauí and Pará as a national cultural manifestation. Originating from Bill 37/2025 by Deputy Ricardo Ayres, the law values this traditional activity, mainly carried out by women, involving the collection, breaking and processing of the coconut for food, handicrafts and production of goods such as oil and soap.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula apresenta resultados do Imóvel da Gente
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva participates in a live ceremony to present the results of the 'Imóvel da Gente' program, which has allocated over 1,700 federal properties since January 2023, benefiting approximately 400,000 families across 625 municipalities. The program exceeded its initial target of 1,600 properties, covering areas such as housing, education, health, and land regularization, totaling more than 18,500 km² of Union land designated for public policies.

item.title: CNI reúne pré-candidatos ao Planalto em evento no dia 22 de junho
item.description: The National Confederation of Industry (CNI) will host the event 'Industry in the Presidential Candidates' Agenda' on June 22 in Brasília, featuring confirmed participation from pre-candidates Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Romeu Zema (Novo), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD). The event will unveil the 'Building Brazil 2050' document, outlining industrial priorities in competitiveness, infrastructure, innovation, and sustainability. The forum aims to align electoral proposals with industry demands to promote sustainable economic growth in Brazil.

item.title: Aprovada pelo Senado, política de recuperação da Caatinga já está em vigor
item.description: The Senate approved and President Lula signed Law 15.430/2026, establishing the National Policy for the Recovery of Caatinga Vegetation. The law mandates coordinated action among federal, state, municipal governments and civil society to combat desertification, control deforestation, and promote sustainable use of the biome, including training and community participation. Although the Chamber proposed a Caatinga Fund, Senator Leila Barros rejected the amendment due to constitutional concerns, leaving the final text without this financial mechanism.

item.title: Motta indica a Alcolumbre que não deve votar pauta-bomba na Câmara
item.description: Chamber President Hugo Motta signaled to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre that he should not vote on the rural debt renegotiation project approved by the Senate, dubbed a 'budget bomb' due to its estimated fiscal impact of R$140 billion over 10 years. Motta said he did not fully know the text and recalled vetoing a similar proposal in 2025 over fiscal concerns, even though it aimed to aid farmers affected by floods in Rio Grande do Sul. The Lula government sought Motta’s support to block the vote in the Chamber, with Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães making an appeal, noting President Lula’s displeasure over the Senate’s approval, especially due to involvement of allied party senators.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro defende Zanatta para vice de Flávio: “Está à altura do cargo”
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro publicly endorsed federal deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) as the vice-presidential candidate on the ticket led by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for the 2026 elections. In a post on X, he stated that Zanatta 'is up to the task' and suggested that criticism of her nomination indicates it is the right choice.

item.title: Comissão da Câmara aprova projeto para financiar tarifa zero com royalties do petróleo
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Urban Development Committee approved a bill by Deputy Jilmar Tatto (PT-SP) allocating a portion of oil royalties to fund zero-fare public transportation. The proposal aims to expand access to urban public transit using national natural resource revenues.

item.title: Em Barcelona para GP da Espanha, pilotos da F1 batem bola e dão palpites sobre Copa do Mundo
item.description: Formula 1 drivers discussed the 2026 World Cup during the Barcelona Grand Prix, sharing their viewing habits and expectations for their national teams. Gabriel Bortoleto said he will watch Brazil's matches when his schedule and sleep allow, despite late-night games in Europe. Other drivers, including Sergio Pérez (Mexico) and Franco Colapinto (Argentina), expressed confidence in their teams' campaigns, while Fernando Alonso said he hopes Spain can reach the final.

item.title: Lula veta projeto que mudava regras de concessão de benefícios sociais para trabalhadores safristas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva fully vetoed Bill 715/23, which would have allowed temporary agricultural workers (safristas) to retain social benefits like Bolsa Família during seasonal employment. The government argued the measure creates mandatory spending without a funding source, making it unconstitutional. The veto will now be reviewed by the National Congress in a joint session.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro defende Júlia Zanatta como vice na chapa de Flávio à Presidência: 'Este é o caminho'
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro defended on social media the nomination of federal deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) as vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket, praising her loyalty and alignment with bolsonarist agendas. The suggestion points toward a potential all-PL ticket, as Flávio has yet to choose his running mate and has expressed preference for a woman. Other names under consideration include Tereza Cristina (PP-MS), Simone Marquetto (PP-SP) and Ciro Nogueira, though some face resistance or political complications.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro atua para reduzir resistência entre mulheres
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro intensified efforts to reduce electoral resistance among women, attending an event with 200 female business leaders and opinion-makers where he reiterated his intention to select a woman as his running mate. He mentioned names such as Tereza Cristina, Simone Marquetto, and Clarissa Tércio, noting that the choice depends on an alliance between the União Brasil and PP federation. Despite emphasizing his commitment to defending women, the Genial/Quaest poll showed he has 24% voting intention among women, compared to 34% among men.

item.title: Flávio apresenta notícia-crime contra Lula por “ameaça”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) filed a criminal complaint with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), accusing him of inciting homicide by strangulation against him. The claim stems from a statement made by Lula on April 2, which Bolsonaro interprets as a direct threat. The case was reported by the news outlet O Antagonista.

item.title: Flávio Dino toma posse como integrante substituto do TSE
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino was sworn in as a substitute member of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on Thursday, June 11, in a formal ceremony at the office of TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques. His appointment, approved by the STF in May, follows the tradition of rotational succession based on judicial seniority. Dino joins Gilmar Mendes and Cristiano Zanin as STF-origin substitutes, while the other jurist substitute position remains vacant.

item.title: Acompanhe ao vivo a abertura da Copa do Mundo de 2026
item.description: The opening ceremony of the 2026 FIFA World Cup takes place this Thursday (June 11) at 2:30 p.m. Brasília time at Estadio Azteca, featuring performances by Shakira, Burna Boy, Belinda, Maná, J Balvin, and Tyla. Following the ceremony, Mexico and South Africa will kick off the tournament, reenacting their 2010 World Cup opener, which ended in a 1-1 draw. Attendees include UEFA President Aleksander Čeferin, Roberto Carlos, Ronaldo, and Luís Figo.

item.title: Senado usa pautas-bomba para constranger o governo
item.description: The Senate is advancing with 'bombshell' proposals totaling R$ 215 billion, aiming to pressure the Lula government in an election year by forcing vetoes that could alienate key voter segments. The opposition already has a narrative ready accusing the government of fiscal irresponsibility and increasing debt, using this move as a tool for political and fiscal manipulation. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Deputados governistas levam aos EUA defesa do Pix e cooperação contra facções, mas não se encontram com Republicanos
item.description: Brazilian ruling-party deputies traveled to the U.S. to advocate for the Pix payment system, seek U.S. cooperation against criminal factions, and raise allegations about ties between Bolsonaro’s family and Banco Master, but failed to secure meetings with Republican officials or the U.S. Department of Justice. They met only with Democratic lawmakers and OEA representatives, presenting documents on sovereignty, extradition requests related to the January 8 attacks, and financial investigations.

item.title: Eleição e briga de Alcolumbre com Lula explicam aprovação de 'pautas-bomba' no Senado
item.description: The Lula government suffered defeats in the Senate with the approval of 'budget-busting' measures, including a rural debt renegotiation that could create a R$140 billion fiscal impact. The administration attributes the loss to senators seeking electoral favors, Davi Alcolumbre's strategy to secure his Senate re-election, and the deteriorated relationship between Lula and Alcolumbre, marked by silence and no dialogue following the rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF.

item.title: Agência dos EUA confirma chegada do El Niño
item.description: The NOAA confirmed the arrival of El Niño in June 2026, with a 63% probability of reaching very strong levels between November 2026 and January 2027, potentially becoming one of the most intense since 1950. In Brazil, the phenomenon is expected to reduce rainfall in the North and Northeast while increasing it in the South, as the Lula government announced a R$ 2 billion environmental prevention package, despite budget cuts to rural insurance programs by the Ministry of Agriculture.

item.title: PT aproveita Copa e lança campanha 'Lula joga pelo Brasil' para reforçar defesa da soberania
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) launched on Thursday, June 11, 2026, the campaign 'Lula plays for Brazil', leveraging the opening of the FIFA World Cup to reinforce the narrative that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defends national sovereignty amid threats of new tariffs from the Donald Trump-led U.S. government. The initiative aims to position Lula as a defender of Brazilian interests in a context of escalating international trade tensions.

item.title: AO VIVO: Abertura da Copa do Mundo; acompanhe
item.description: The 2026 World Cup opens live on Thursday, June 11, at 2:30 PM Brasília time at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, followed by Mexico vs. South Africa at 4:00 PM. Parallel opening ceremonies will take place in Toronto, Canada, and Los Angeles, USA, on Friday, June 12, with subsequent matches: Canada vs. Bosnia and Herzegovina and USA vs. Paraguay. Brazil debuts against Morocco on Saturday, June 13, at 7:00 PM in New York/New Jersey, aiming for a sixth title.

item.title: Azarão vira opção menos problemática para acabar com crise sobre chapa do PL no Rio
item.description: Carlos Portinho, the PL Senate leader, has emerged as the least problematic option for the party's Rio de Janeiro Senate slate amid internal disputes over candidate selection. Though seen as a longshot for not appealing to the radical electorate, his candidacy is viewed as strategic to avoid conflict between allies like Sóstenes Cavalcante and Carlos Jordy, and to spare Flávio Bolsonaro from having to choose between two Chamber allies. The decision may be delayed until just before the convention.

item.title: CNC chama presidenciáveis para defender agenda do comércio
item.description: The National Confederation of Commerce (CNC) has invited the four leading presidential candidates for an event on July 8 in Brasília to present its institutional agenda on commerce, services, and tourism. The agenda calls for tax and competitive parity between domestic firms and foreign platforms, stricter enforcement against piracy and smuggling, and a national AI program for micro and small businesses. The meeting serves as a pre-campaign sectoral economic hearing to gauge candidates’ willingness to adopt a platform combining national commerce protection, illegal market repression, and digital inclusion.

item.title: “Lula quieto é um grande poeta”, diz Coronel Assis
item.description: Deputy Coronel Assis (PL-MT), rapporteur of the PEC on reducing the age of criminal responsibility, strongly criticized President Lula during an interview on the Meio-Dia program in Brasília, stating that 'Quiet Lula is a great poet'. The comment came after Assis watched a video in which Lula mentioned the possibility of sending alerts to stolen cell phones.

item.title: Três meses depois, PEC do fim da reeleição para presidente é ‘esquecida’ no Senado
item.description: Three months after its introduction, the PEC seeking to end presidential reelection remains stalled, awaiting dispatch from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Led by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and backed by 29 lawmakers, the proposal received only 15 favorable votes out of 64 public opinions in the Senate system. The amendment would modify Article 14 of the Constitution to allow reelection only for state governors and mayors, excluding the president.

item.title: “As declarações desse presidente nos dão nojo”, diz relator da PEC da maioridade penal
item.description: Colonel Assis (PL-MT), rapporteur of the proposal to lower the age of criminal responsibility to 16 for serious crimes, harshly criticized President Lula during an interview on the Meio-Dia em Brasília program, stating that the president's remarks on public security and robbery make him feel 'disgusted'. The proposal was approved for admissibility by the CCJ of the Chamber last Wednesday, the 10th.

item.title: Lula chega à Copa em vantagem no placar, mas jogo eleitoral ‘só acaba quando termina’
item.description: Lula enters the World Cup with an electoral advantage, as a Quaest poll shows 47% approval and 48% disapproval, reversing a months-long negative trend. His main rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, faces pressure from leaked audios with Daniel Vorcaro and the inclusion of Pix in Trump’s tariff investigations, enabling the PT to launch slogans like 'O Pix é do Brasil' and jersey-inspired merchandise linking Lula to national patriotism.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula anuncia dados do desmatamento na Amazônia e no Cerrado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced deforestation data for the Amazon and Cerrado at an OTCA event in Brasília, attended by Environment Minister João Paulo Capobianco and Science and Technology Minister Luciana Santos. The Deter and Prodes monitoring systems were presented to assess deforestation trends under his administration. The event underscores the government's commitment to environmental transparency and combating illegal deforestation.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro apoia Júlia Zanatta para vice na chapa de Flávio
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro endorsed federal deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) as vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) 2026 ticket, praising her loyalty, congressional performance, and opposition to the left. Zanatta responded that 'the thing is taking shape,' signaling progress. Senator Tereza Cristina (PP-MS), former agriculture minister under Jair Bolsonaro, is also being considered, with Flávio saying her selection would be 'everyone’s dream.'

item.title: O número mais preocupante para Flávio Bolsonaro na nova Quaest não é o mais óbvio
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that, although Flávio Bolsonaro remains Lula's main rival in 2026, his biggest concern is not the drop in voting intentions but the rise in rejection and loss of independent voters. Rejection reflects solidified negative perceptions, which are harder to reverse than temporary shifts in vote intention. Much of this wear is driving voters toward indecision or blank/null votes, with issues like the 'tariff shock' and his association with Donald Trump deepening discomfort among independents.

item.title: Lula, quatro anos depois e dez pontos a menos contra um Bolsonaro
item.description: According to the Genial/Quaest poll, Lula leads with 44% voting intentions against Flávio Bolsonaro, who has 38%, a six-point advantage. A month earlier, the two were technically tied, with 42% for Lula and 41% for the senator.

item.title: Lula faz comercial no horário nobre sobre bondades em ano eleitoral
item.description: The federal government aired a 1-minute commercial during prime time on open TV to highlight Lula’s social and labor programs, including debt renegotiation, Farmácia Popular, CNH Social, and the push to end the 6x1 work schedule. The ad links these initiatives to the slogan 'on the side of the Brazilian people' and was broadcast during high-audience news programs, with Lula also sharing it on social media.

item.title: Dr. Hiran critica desincompatibilização em eleição suplementar de Roraima
item.description: Senator Dr. Hiran (PP-RR) criticized judicial decisions requiring candidates to resign from office months before the Roraima supplementary election, arguing that ordinary election rules do not apply to a vote triggered by the cassation of the governor and vice-governor. He claimed that candidates like former Boa Vista mayor Arthur Henrique could not have anticipated the election and thus could not comply with disaffiliation timelines. Hiran accused Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino of improperly interfering in the electoral process and blocking the candidate's registration.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Indisposto com Lula, Alcolumbre maneja pauta do Senado contra planos do governo
item.description: Davi Alcolumbre, dissatisfied with the Lula government, has been delaying and modifying key Executive proposals in the Senate, such as the PEC to reduce the workweek to 6x1, despite lacking the power to block it entirely. He also advanced rural debt renegotiation projects and sought to overturn Lula’s Marco Civil da Internet decree, demonstrating efforts to hinder the government’s agenda in an election year.
